decisions.descriptionMarkdown:
cargo-dist stays the owner of the release workflow, archives, checksums, installers and the GitHub Release. This epic changes only its configuration (`dist-workspace.toml`) and regenerates `release.yml` with dist 0.33.0:

- **Install path** `["$RAYX_HOME/bin", "~/.rayx/bin"]`: `rayx` lives in its own directory, not in rustup's `~/.cargo/bin` (which `rustup self uninstall` deletes). The installers add it to PATH (`HKCU\Environment\Path` with a `WM_SETTINGCHANGE` broadcast on Windows; an `env` script sourced from the shell profiles on Unix) and write the receipt `axoupdater` reads, so `src/update.rs` needs no change.
- **Windows ARM64** builds on `windows-2022` with host `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` through `[dist.github-custom-runners]`: MSVC's ARM64 cross tools, no cargo-xwin container, where `aws-lc-sys` (pulled in by `axoupdater` -> `axoasset` -> `reqwest` default TLS) is known to fail. Not `windows-11-arm`: dist publishes no Windows ARM64 build of itself, so its installer cannot run there. ARM64 Linux already builds natively on dist's default `ubuntu-22.04-arm`.
- **Attestations** (`github-attestations = true`): free Sigstore provenance for every artifact on a public repository.
- **`pr-run-mode = "upload"`**: every pull request builds all six targets, so a broken target shows before a tag, not after.

**Windows ARM64 fallback order** if `windows-2022` fails: (1) a `github-build-setup` step that puts LLVM's `clang-cl` on PATH; (2) an upstream axoasset PR that lets dependents choose the TLS backend (e.g. rustls with `ring`), used through a pinned `[patch]` under `d-dependency-sources` until released; (3) replacing axoupdater only with the owner's decision. Each step is a recorded finding and a scope amendment.
decisions.invariantsMarkdown:
- `release.yml` changes only through `dist generate`; no `allow-dirty`.
- Asset names and URLs stay `rayx-cli-<triple>.<ext>`, `rayx-cli-installer.{sh,ps1}`, under `releases/download/v<version>/` and `releases/latest/download/`.
- The build runs on GitHub-hosted runners only.
decisions.rationaleMarkdown: Research 2026-10-14: dist 0.33.0 (2026-09-10) is the latest release with no breaking changes from 0.32.0; the project is community-maintained and active, Astral's fork is archived. axoupdater 0.10.2 is current. On Windows, axoupdater renames the running `rayx.exe` aside, runs the release's PowerShell installer with the install directory from the receipt, and restores the old exe on failure. The cargo-xwin `aws-lc-sys` failures (dist issues #1576, #1633, #1825) need `XWIN_CROSS_COMPILER=clang`, which dist does not expose. A switch to `ring` is impossible from this crate alone because axoasset enables reqwest's default TLS (rustls with aws-lc-rs) and features only add. Keeping `pr-run-mode = "upload"` costs extra minutes per PR on a public repository with free hosted minutes, which the owner's requirement that every platform builds on remote runners justifies.

decisions.descriptionMarkdown:
release-plz turns Conventional Commits into releases. On every push to `main` it keeps a release PR open with the version bump in `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` and the new `CHANGELOG.md` section (git-cliff). When the release PR is merged, `release-plz release` pushes the tag `vX.Y.Z`, and the tag starts dist's `release.yml`, which builds and creates the GitHub Release with notes from the matching `CHANGELOG.md` section. release-plz runs with `git_only = true` (versions come from tags, nothing goes to crates.io) and `git_release_enable = false` (dist owns the GitHub Release).

It authenticates with the fine-grained PAT secret `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` (resource owner `rayx-ui`, only `RayX.CLI`, Contents and Pull requests read/write): events made with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` start no workflows, so with it the release PR would get no CI (`ci.yml` runs on pull requests only) and the tag would not start `release.yml`.

Versions start at **1.0.0** (`Cargo.toml` and a hand-written first `CHANGELOG.md` section). After that `fix` bumps the patch, `feat` the minor and `feat!`/`BREAKING CHANGE` the major version. If release-plz cannot release the first version from a history without tags, the by-hand fallback (`git tag v1.0.0`, push) cuts it and release-plz continues from that tag.
decisions.invariantsMarkdown:
- Tags have the form `v<semver>` and come from release-plz or the documented by-hand fallback, never from another tool.
- `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` is the only release secret; it lives in GitHub Actions, never in `rayx` or the repository.
- `ci.yml` stays pull-request only; `release-plz.yml` is the one workflow that runs on pushes to `main`, and it runs no tests.
decisions.rationaleMarkdown: release-plz is the Rust-native choice (release-please handles Cargo less well; cargo-release, which dist's docs suggest, needs a local run per release). The owner chose a fine-grained PAT over a GitHub App on 2026-10-14 as simpler; the cost is that release PRs and tags appear as the owner and releases stop silently when the token expires, so `docs/releasing.md` covers rotation. `dispatch-releases` was rejected: it removes the tag trigger release-plz relies on.

decisions.descriptionMarkdown:
One Cargo package `rayx-cli` at the repository root stays: library `rayx_cli` (`src/lib.rs`) and binary `rayx` (`src/main.rs`, which only calls `rayx_cli::run`), with the modules `cli`, `host`, `project`, `setup` (with `setup::wsl`), `doctor`, `update`, `app`, `fmt` and `wsl`; integration test groups are `tests/<feature>.rs`, fixture projects `tests/fixtures/<name>/` with their own empty `[workspace]` table. A new crate is added only when a second consumer needs a module.

What changes is where dependencies may come from. The rule is that anyone who clones the public repository can build it on any machine or CI runner:

- allowed: crates.io; public git repositories over `https://` pinned to a `rev` (Gpux, `rayx-ui/Gpux`, is public under Apache-2.0); `[patch]` for a recorded reason, with a comment linking the upstream issue or PR, removed once upstream releases the change;
- forbidden: `path` dependencies on sibling checkouts (`../Gpux`, `../RayX`), git dependencies on a moving `branch`/`tag`, any dependency on the private `rayx-ui/RayX` or another private repository, `[replace]`.

`tests/dependency_sources.rs` enforces it with a rule function tested on sample manifests and applied to the real one.
decisions.invariantsMarkdown:
- A clean clone builds with network access to crates.io and public GitHub only.
- No module reads a compile-time path to decide what to work on (`env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")` only in tests).
decisions.rationaleMarkdown: Supersedes the 2026-10-08 single-package decision, whose invariant allowed crates.io only with no `git` and no `[patch]`. The owner (2026-10-14) wants agents able to fix and refactor through upstream code instead of band-aids, and Gpux is now public. The part of the old rule that protects buildability stays: a private or path dependency fails on every CI runner and for every other user.

decisions.descriptionMarkdown:
`setup::wsl` runs on Windows only and drives `wsl.exe`: `wsl --version` for WSL 2, `wsl -l -q` for the distribution, `wsl --install -d Ubuntu-24.04` when missing, and `id -un` to detect a missing default user. Scripts inside the distribution run with `--exec bash -lc`.

The Linux `rayx` is the running version installed by that release's own installer: when `$HOME/.rayx/bin/rayx --version` does not print `rayx <version>`, the distribution runs `curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://github.com/rayx-ui/RayX.CLI/releases/download/v<version>/rayx-cli-installer.sh | sh` non-interactively. The installer picks the musl archive for the architecture, verifies it, installs into `~/.rayx/bin`, adds it to PATH and writes the receipt, so `rayx self update` works inside WSL. `RAYX_WSL_BINARY` copies a local build to `$HOME/.rayx/bin/rayx` through `wslpath` instead (no receipt). The inner run is `$HOME/.rayx/bin/rayx setup <same flags>` with inherited stdio.

`--clone` copies only the current checkout (translating `D:\...` to `/mnt/d/...` and keeping its branch) and lets Cargo fetch every dependency inside WSL. `rayx wsl status` and `rayx wsl compact` are unchanged.
decisions.invariantsMarkdown:
- Never enable WSL sparse disks.
- Never delete anything outside the listed build-output directories, and never without confirmation unless `--yes` was given.
- Never follow a manifest's `path` dependencies to clone, copy or download another repository.
- `--check` downloads and installs nothing.
decisions.rationaleMarkdown: Supersedes the 2026-10-08 WSL decision only in how the Linux binary arrives: it extracted `rayx-cli-<arch>-unknown-linux-musl.tar.xz` into `~/.local/bin` with no receipt, so `self update` inside WSL refused. Installing the way users install keeps one install path and one update path on every OS (owner, 2026-10-14). The rest of the decision is restated unchanged.

decisions.descriptionMarkdown: RayX CI installs a pinned **release** of `rayx` instead of compiling a pinned commit: `RAYX_CLI_VERSION: 1.0.0` and the shell installer of that version, with `~/.rayx/bin` on `GITHUB_PATH`. Moving the pin is the paired RayX change for any CLI change RayX relies on (grammar, flags, artifact layout, `[package.metadata.rayx]`), now done by releasing the CLI first. RayX's docs install from the release one-liners.
decisions.invariantsMarkdown: - RayX CI never installs `rayx` from a moving branch or `latest`; it names a version.
decisions.rationaleMarkdown: RayX's own 2026-10-08 decision already says to use the release installer once a release exists. A prebuilt install takes seconds instead of a release compile per job.
